Galaxies at 100,000 light-years to the metre

The Milky Way is a spiral a metre across over a round glass table; the Sun, a glint 27 cm from its centre; the Magellanic Clouds float 1.6 and 2 m away. Andromeda is 25 m off, 1.5 m across: the Local Group spreads over about 100 m, joined by walkways. Bike trails go to the galaxies hundreds of metres away (the Virgo Cluster, 535 m), roads and a car to the clusters kilometres off (Coma, 3.2 km), a jet to runways by the most distant galaxies, 320 km away. The 43,000 galaxies of the 2MASS Redshift Survey trace the cosmic web to 24 km; the cosmic microwave background, the edge of what we can see, surrounds everything 457 km away.

WASD walk  ·  drag to look  ·  E about what you look at  ·  T teleport  ·  E beside the bike, car, helicopter or jet to ride  ·  F fly (space / C up and down, =− speed, up to 100 km/s)  ·  P paths  ·  L labels  ·  H readout  ·  M sitting  ·  R back to the desk
In VR: left stick walk or fly, right stick turn, B fly / land (right stick up/down to climb), Y flying speed, A or right trigger: about what you look at, X labels, click the left stick: sitting; teleport from the panel on your left wrist

Galaxy positions: the 2MASS Redshift Survey (Huchra et al. 2012), distances from redshift; named galaxies from NED and the literature. Far distances are where galaxies are now (comoving). Click to begin.
